title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 55 (Issue and Redemption of Preference Shares)

content.overview: Section 55 restricts a company limited by shares from issuing irredeemable preference shares. Preference shares must be redeemable within a period not exceeding twenty years from the date of issue (with a longer period permitted for infrastructure projects as prescribed). Redemption must be out of profits available for dividend or out of the proceeds of a fresh issue, and fully paid-up shares only may be redeemed. A capital redemption reserve is required where redemption is out of profits.
content.glance: No irredeemable preference shares; redeem within 20 years (infrastructure exception); redeem only fully paid shares out of profits or fresh issue; capital redemption reserve when out of profits.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 55 (Issue and redemption of preference shares). A company limited by shares must not issue irredeemable preference shares. Preference shares ordinarily must be redeemable within 20 years of issue; a company engaged in infrastructure projects may use a longer prescribed period not exceeding 30 years, subject to prescribed annual redemption requirements and the preference shareholders' option. Only fully paid-up preference shares may be redeemed, and redemption must be funded from profits otherwise available for dividend or proceeds of a fresh issue made for redemption. Where redemption is funded from profits, a sum equal to the nominal amount redeemed must be transferred to the capital redemption reserve. Any premium payable on redemption must be provided from profits or the securities premium account as permitted by the section. If the company cannot redeem or pay dividend in accordance with the terms, subsection (3) provides a route involving consent of holders of three-fourths in value and Tribunal approval to issue further redeemable preference shares for the amount due, without prejudice to the rights of holders who do not consent. Verify current prescribed infrastructure rules and the terms of issue.

sections.heading: No irredeemable preference shares and ordinary period
sections.body: A company limited by shares must not issue irredeemable preference shares. Preference shares ordinarily must be redeemable within 20 years from issue.

sections.heading: Infrastructure exception
sections.body: For a company engaged in infrastructure projects, a longer prescribed period not exceeding 30 years may apply, subject to prescribed annual redemption requirements and the preference shareholders' option. Verify the current rule for the precise schedule and conditions.

sections.heading: Permitted source and fully paid status
sections.body: Only fully paid-up preference shares may be redeemed. Redemption must be out of profits otherwise available for dividend or proceeds of a fresh issue made for redemption.

sections.heading: Capital redemption reserve and premium
sections.body: Where redemption is out of profits, transfer a sum equal to the nominal amount redeemed to the capital redemption reserve account. Any premium payable on redemption must be provided from profits or the securities premium account as permitted by section 55.

sections.heading: Inability to redeem
sections.body: Where the company cannot redeem preference shares or pay dividend in accordance with the terms, subsection (3) provides a route, subject to consent of holders of three-fourths in value and Tribunal approval, for issuing further redeemable preference shares for the amount due. Apply the statutory conditions and preserve the rights of non-consenting holders.

provisions.title: Issue and redemption of preference shares

examples.title: Valid redeemable issue
examples.body: A company issues preference shares redeemable in 15 years, to be redeemed out of profits with CRR created. Section 55 is complied with.

examples.title: Irredeemable attempt
examples.body: Articles purport to authorise irredeemable preference shares. Section 55 prohibits such issue.

hypotheticals.question: A company redeems preference shares out of profits. What reserve transfer is required?
hypotheticals.analysis: A sum equal to the nominal amount of the shares redeemed must be transferred to the capital redemption reserve account.

hypotheticals.question: A company cannot redeem preference shares on the due date. Can it automatically extend the redemption date?
hypotheticals.analysis: No automatic extension should be assumed. Analyse subsection (3), including consent of holders of three-fourths in value and Tribunal approval, and verify all statutory conditions.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming special resolution can authorise irredeemable preference shares.
Redeeming partly paid preference shares or using any funding source.
misconceptions.correction: Only fully paid-up shares may be redeemed, and funding must come from profits available for dividend or a fresh issue for redemption.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the premium and capital-redemption-reserve requirements.
misconceptions.correction: Apply the section's separate premium funding rule and transfer nominal value to CRR where redemption is out of profits.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the infrastructure exception as an unrestricted 30-year period.
misconceptions.correction: The longer period is prescribed, capped at 30 years and subject to prescribed annual redemption requirements.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the ordinary maximum redemption period?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Twenty years from issue; an infrastructure-project exception may allow a prescribed longer period not exceeding 30 years, subject to conditions.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When is a capital redemption reserve required?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: When preference shares are redeemed out of profits, a sum equal to the nominal amount redeemed must be transferred to CRR.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What happens if the company cannot redeem under the terms?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Subsection (3) provides a conditional route involving consent of holders of three-fourths in value and Tribunal approval for a further issue of redeemable preference shares.
